findings.claim: The ruling's real branch is (c), which costs more than the defect it removes. The per-sub-agent branch is dead: the documented `agents:` keys at docs/reference/archon/workflow-language.md:666 are description, prompt, model, tools, disallowedTools, skills and maxTurns, with no server list. After D-43 (CONTEXT.md:60), the speccer holding fence-scratch and fence-spike can only write under gauntlet/scratch and run a command fixed in the fence. The only harm left is that a prompt rule (spec-review-design.md:520) stops the speccer from doing the spiker's work itself.
findings.failure_scenario: spec-review-design.md:239 requires a stub proof for every spec in every block, and :242 requires `measure` answers verbatim. Today the speccer gets both inside one `file` turn through Agent. Under (c) the speccer's reply can only start a spiker node. So every round needs an Opus resume turn that briefs the spiker, then a spiker node session, then a second Opus resume turn that writes `<slug>.N.txt`. Speccer turns per round roughly double, which is token waste under CLAUDE.md 1.3. The thing saved is a confinement the D-43 fixed-command fence already makes harmless.

findings.claim: Applying (c) as written breaks hearing-loop lines that the ruling leaves unaddressed. `file` (:398-415) has no output_format that could carry a spike request. The ledger has no 'spike pending' state. One spiker node drops the parallel per-set spikers of :24 and :249-250. The spiker's results can reach the next `file` turn only through `$LOOP_PREV` of a node that its own `when:` skips in most iterations, the pattern G-26/D-28 and G-72/D-49 already ruled defective.
findings.failure_scenario: The speccer's turn asks for spikes and writes no `<slug>.N.txt`. `ready` (:417-422) then answers owed=speccer, and screen and the arbiter are skipped. The spiker node runs, and the next iteration's `file` prompt must bind `$LOOP_PREV.<spiker>.output`. In any iteration where no spike was asked, that binding reads a skipped node. Each spike cycle also adds a loop iteration, and under D-41 (CONTEXT.md:58) iterations are what the 200 bound and `cap` now count. A spec needing a spike every round therefore reaches the owner ask at about 100 rounds, not the 200 the comment at :374 states. Two related sets that ran in parallel now run one after the other across iterations.
